title: Expected value of Gaussian rounding
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $G$ be a weighted directed graph on $n$ vertices, and assign to each vertex $v$ a unit vector $U_v\in\mathbb R^n$. If $g$ has independent standard Gaussian coordinates and each vertex is rounded according to the sign of $\langle U_v,g\rangle$, then the expected cut value is $\displaystyle\sum_{v,w}w(v,w)\,\frac{\arccos\langle U_v,U_w\rangle}{\pi}$, where the cut value sums the weights of ordered pairs whose rounded labels differ.
hypotheses_covered: $G$ is a weighted directed graph on the $n$ vertices; its real weights are unrestricted.
